## Log & Execution
> Quick notes, terminal outputs, server paths, and thoughts during the day.

The first thing i will do is download the database, and look at the structure.
```bash
wget https://github.com/pr2database/pr2database/releases/download/v5.1.1/pr2_version_5.1.1_SSU_taxo_long.fasta.gz
```
Looking at the first header and sequence I see this:
```
>AB353770.1.1740_U|18S_rRNA|nucleus||Eukaryota|TSAR|Alveolata|Dinoflagellata|Dinophyceae|Peridiniales|Kryptoperidiniaceae|Unruhdinium|Unruhdinium_kevei 
```
The header is made up by the following metrics:
- Accession
- Molecule type
- Cellular location
- Empty field
- 9 taxonomy levels (Domain -> Species)


This is somewhat different from the Silva db
```
>AY846379.1.1791 Eukaryota;Archaeplastida;Chloroplastida;Chlorophyta;Chlorophyceae;Sphaeropleales;Monoraphidium;Monoraphidium sp. Itas 9/21 14-6w
```
This is only made up of the:
- Accession
- 7-8 taxonomy levels

The columns in the PR2 database have 1-2 extra taxonomy levels, the CABO-16S article (mentioned in [Project Timeline & Planning](/Project%20Timeline%20&%20Planning.md)) drops these specific levels, as you want the combined database to be consistent. Silva already contains 18S sequences, but as PR2 states themselves: "Silva tries to be as extensive as possible while PR2 only includes sequences that have been annotated by experts." - https://pr2database.github.io/pr2database/articles/pr2_02A_silva.html. This means that the 18S sequences from PR2 could potentially be more secure. This means that there might be duplicate values, something i will keep in mind. I will have to check for duplicates based on similar sequences instead of species naming conventions. I will update my python library to be able to merge different databases. One of the other notable differences is that Silva is in RNA format (it was U in the sequences), while PR2 uses T, so in DNA format. I will need to implement it in a way that turns both databases into the same format (RNA in this case as Silva will be our base db)

## Notes & Blockers
The start of a new milestone starts today, this means i will start tinkering with the different reference databases. To see how they both fit on marine data / universal primer sequenced data. This will start first by creating a new custom database that contains both 16S and 18S data. Savont naturally already supports a reference database with good 16S coverage, like Silva. So today will be finding ways to combine these 2 databases into one, while remaining functional. I will combine the Silva database, that is already supported in Savont, with PR2 a reference database often used for 18S amplicon data.
